text.tspan: Let's now step back and take a better look at how biology actually carries out transcription.
So far we've been assuming that the promoter is the only control mechanism responsible
for launching RNA Polymerase and transcribing a gene. In eukaryotes, which include all
organisms except bacteria and archaea, distant parts of DNA are known to play a central
role in transcription initiation. Like promoters, these are non-coding sequences, known as
enhancers. However, they can be hundreds of thousands of base pairs away from a gene.
How these sequences can benefit precise gene regulation despite being so far away
has been a puzzle in biology for many years.
